saw.short: Celebrity Traitors fans guessed the murder before it aired
saw.headline: Celebrity Traitors fans *guessed the murder* before it aired
saw.what: Miranda Hart was murdered on Friday's episode. The night before, some viewers guessed from King Kenny's pen position that he was writing an “M”, and they were right. The finale is reported for Fri 30 Oct, 8pm on BBC One.
saw.why: Fans treat tiny details as clues, and a correct guess becomes the story. Expect more of it before the finale.

saw.short: Strictly's wrong on-screen score gets spotted live
saw.headline: Strictly's *wrong on-screen score* gets spotted live
saw.what: On Saturday the graphic showed Shirley Ballas's 6 for Lacey Turner and Vito Coppola as a 7, so the total read 29 instead of 28. Emma Willis apologised on air. On Sunday Shaun Wright-Phillips and Alexis Warr went home.
saw.why: Viewers watch with a phone in hand, so any slip becomes a post within minutes.
saw.source: Radio Times, 24 Oct; Digital Spy, 25 Oct

saw.short: SNL UK's Cynthia Erivo plays Glinda in “Nigerian Wicked”
saw.headline: SNL UK's Cynthia Erivo plays Glinda in *“Nigerian Wicked”*
saw.what: On Saturday's SNL UK, host Cynthia Erivo played Glinda in a Nollywood-style parody of Wicked, with Ayoade Bamgboye as Elphaba. Her monologue joked about Bake Off: “I've got a soggy bottom, and I'm freaking stressed!”
saw.why: A huge film plus a UK TV staple makes easy clips to share.
saw.credit: Sky / SNL UK via AV Club

saw.short: Prince William is mistaken for Prince on Graham Norton
saw.headline: Prince William is *mistaken for Prince* on Graham Norton
saw.what: On The Graham Norton Show on Friday, Prince William said a man in Somerset asked “When are you going to sing?” because he thought he was Prince, the singer. He also said his DJ name was “DJ Xara with an X, it wasn't good.”
saw.why: A self-deprecating royal story is easy to quote and share.

platform.short: Snap's survey: 56% of AI users find fully AI content “soulless”
platform.headline: Snap's survey: *56% of AI users* find fully AI content “soulless”
platform.what: Snap's survey of more than 4,200 AI users found 48% use AI daily and 56% see 100% AI-generated content as “soulless”. 70% find personal data in hyper-personalised AI ads intrusive. It is Snap's own report.
platform.why: Even regular AI users want a human hand. Clearly human-made content has an edge.

platform.short: Instagram's Rings creator awards return for a second year
platform.headline: Instagram's *Rings* creator awards return for year two
platform.what: Instagram's Rings awards are back. A panel of judges, including Donatella Versace and Adam Mosseri, nominates and picks the winners, so creators can't enter. Winners get in-app promotion and a physical gold ring.
platform.why: A creator award with no entry form. Brands can't buy a place, only watch who is chosen.

platform.short: Meta's Muse app tops 10m downloads, with shopping a common use
platform.headline: Meta's *Muse* app tops 10m downloads
platform.what: Mark Zuckerberg said Muse has had more than 10m downloads since its US and Canada launch last month. Shopping is the most common use, with more than 25% of users asking for deal and purchase help. No UK launch is confirmed.
platform.why: AI assistants are turning into shopping tools, but UK brands can't plan around Muse yet.
